_hinweis: Vocabulary step on /professores/licao and /licao: for each A1 word field in kursinhalte.json (bloecke[].wortschatz, keys must match exactly) a task for the learners and its words. A word that is a lemma of the A1 list (src/content/lexicon/a1.json) gets its o/a, plural and example sentence from there; a noun the list does not have may be written with its article ("a carta", "o NIF"); phrases without an entry (Olá!, letters) are shown as written here. Word fields without an entry only show the general task.

ptBR.note: Brazil says ônibus, trem, celular, café da manhã, banheiro and você with friends; Portugal: autocarro, comboio, telemóvel, pequeno-almoço, casa de banho, tu.

Greetings.aufgabe: Walk around the room. Say hello to three people, ask how they are and say goodbye: once with tu, once with o senhor / a senhora.
woerter: Bem, obrigado. / Bem, obrigada. E tu?

Countries and nationalities.aufgabe: Ask your partner: «De onde és?» – «Sou de …». Show the country on a map or on your phone.

Languages.aufgabe: Ask each other: «Que línguas falas?» Everyone says two languages. Write all the languages of the class on the board. Languages have no capital letter in Portuguese.

The alphabet.aufgabe: Spell your first name and your surname. Your partner writes them down and reads them back.

Numbers.aufgabe: Count round the class to 20, then in tens to 100. In pairs, dictate three phone numbers to each other. In Portugal mobile numbers have nine digits and are often read in groups of three: 912 345 678.

Address.aufgabe: Ask each other: «Onde moras?» Write down your partner's address: street, number, floor, postcode and town. A Portuguese address reads like this: Rua das Flores, 12, 3.º esq., 4050-262 Porto.

Email.aufgabe: Dictate an email address to your partner. Your partner writes it down and reads it back.

Forms: nome, apelido, morada, NIF.aufgabe: In pairs, fill in a form for each other: ask, listen, write. Many Portuguese people have several surnames: the last one is the one used most.

Family.aufgabe: Draw your family tree and explain it to your partner: «Esta é a minha mãe …»

Friends.aufgabe: Tell your partner about a good friend: name, where they are from, what you do together.

Describing people.aufgabe: Describe a person in the class. The others guess who it is.

Rooms.aufgabe: Draw your flat or house. Show your partner around: «Esta é a cozinha …»

Furniture.aufgabe: Say what is in your living room. Your partner draws it.

Colours.aufgabe: Find something in the room for every colour and say: «A mochila é azul.» Watch the ending: o carro vermelho, a casa vermelha.

Hunting for a flat.aufgabe: Role play: one person phones about a flat ad, the other is the senhorio. Ask about the rent, the rooms and when you can see it. T1 = one bedroom, T2 = two.

Food and drink.aufgabe: Write your shopping list for the weekend. Read it to your partner.

At the café (pequeno-almoço, bica, paste.aufgabe: Role play at the café: one person is the empregado de mesa, one orders pequeno-almoço. Then ask for the bill.

Shopping phrases.aufgabe: Play shop: one person sells, one person buys. Use «uma garrafa de», «um pacote de», «um quilo de».

Prices in euros.aufgabe: Write prices on cards. Your partner asks: «Quanto custa?» and you read the price: 3,50 € = três euros e cinquenta (cêntimos).

Daily routine.aufgabe: Tell your partner about your morning: «Levanto-me às sete. Depois …» The pronoun comes after the verb.

Days and times.aufgabe: Ask each other: «O que fazes na segunda-feira?» Make a plan for the week together. Days have no capital letter in Portuguese.

Meals.aufgabe: Ask three people: «A que horas almoças?» Compare with your country. In Portugal lunch is often from one o'clock and dinner around eight.

Hobbies.aufgabe: Ask three people: «O que fazes no teu tempo livre?» Find one hobby you share.
woerter: O que fazes no teu tempo livre?

Sports.aufgabe: Mime a sport. The others guess it: «Jogas futebol?»

Weekend plans.aufgabe: Plan a weekend together: no sábado de manhã, no sábado à tarde, no domingo.

Places in town.aufgabe: Draw a small map of your town. Your partner asks: «Há um banco aqui perto?»

Transport: autocarro, comboio, metro.aufgabe: Ask three people: «Como vais para o trabalho?» Count the answers.

Directions.aufgabe: Use the map. Explain the way from the station to the bank. Your partner follows it with a finger.

Tickets and passes.aufgabe: Role play at the ticket office: buy a return ticket to Coimbra, then ask about a monthly pass.
woerter: Um bilhete para Coimbra, por favor.

The body.aufgabe: One person says a body part, everyone touches it: «A cabeça!» Then a learner takes over.

Symptoms.aufgabe: Mime an illness. The others guess: «Dói-te a cabeça?» «Tens febre?»

The pharmacy.aufgabe: Role play at the farmácia: say what is wrong and ask for something for it. The pharmacist asks if you have a prescription.
woerter: Tem alguma coisa para a tosse?

Centro de saúde and número de utente.aufgabe: Role play at the centro de saúde: the receptionist asks for your número de utente, the doctor asks what is wrong. To ask for an appointment you can also phone or use SNS 24.
woerter: O que é que se passa?

Everyday activities.aufgabe: Mime something. The others guess with estar a + infinitive: «Estás a cozinhar?» «Sim, estou a cozinhar.»

Plans.aufgabe: Ask your partner: «O que vais fazer no fim de semana?» Tell the class one thing.

Time words: amanhã, na próxima semana.aufgabe: Make a timeline on the board: agora, hoje, logo à tarde, amanhã, na próxima semana. Everyone adds one sentence.

Jobs.aufgabe: Mime a job. The others guess: «És professora?» Portuguese has no um or uma here: Sou enfermeiro.

The workplace.aufgabe: Say where people work: «Um professor trabalha numa escola.» Your partner names another job.

Working hours.aufgabe: Ask each other: «A que horas começas? A que horas acabas?» Write down the times. Who works by turnos, who has a horário fixo?

Contract and salary.aufgabe: Read the words together. Then role play: a new worker asks the chefe about the contract, the salary and the holidays. This is language practice, not advice about your own contract.

Clothes.aufgabe: Describe what a person in the class is wearing. The others guess who it is.

Sizes and colours.aufgabe: Role play in a clothes shop: ask for another size or another colour.

At the checkout.aufgabe: Role play at the till: the customer pays, the shop assistant asks how and if they want the NIF on the receipt.

Months and seasons.aufgabe: Line up by birthday, janeiro to dezembro. Everyone says their month. Months have no capital letter in Portuguese.

Holidays: Natal, Páscoa, 25 de Abril.aufgabe: Tell your partner about a holiday in your country: When is it? What do people do? Then name one you know in Portugal.

Invitations.aufgabe: Write a short invitation to a party. Your partner says yes or no and gives a reason.

Offices: Junta de Freguesia, Finanças, A.aufgabe: Role play at the Junta de Freguesia: ask where the right desk is and what papers you need. The other person works there. This is language practice: what you really need is on the office's own website.

Forms: NIF, NISS, morada.aufgabe: Swap forms with your partner and check them: is every box filled in? Is the date right, day first (03/11/2026)?

Making an appointment (marcação).aufgabe: Role play on the phone: ask for a marcação (at Finanças, the centro de saúde or the hairdresser). Find a day and a time that works.
woerter: Queria fazer uma marcação, por favor.
